slot.brief: Two wires of the same material but different lengths and radii under the same load; compare their elongations using Y = (F/A)(L/ΔL).

stem: Two wires P and Q are made of the same material and carry the same tensile load. Their lengths are $0.6$ m and $0.9$ m, and their radii are $0.4$ mm and $0.6$ mm, respectively. Find $\dfrac{\Delta l_P}{\Delta l_Q}$.

verdicts.working: For the same load and material, \(\Delta l\propto L/r^2\). Thus \(\Delta l_P/\Delta l_Q=(0.6/0.4^2)/(0.9/0.6^2)=3/2\).

working:
$\Delta l=\dfrac{FL}{\pi r^2Y}$
$\dfrac{\Delta l_P}{\Delta l_Q}=\dfrac{0.6}{0.9}\left(\dfrac{0.6}{0.4}\right)^2=\dfrac{3}{2}$

Independent check: For the same load and material, \(\Delta l\propto L/r^2\). Thus \(\Delta l_P/\Delta l_Q=(0.6/0.4^2)/(0.9/0.6^2)=3/2\).
solution:
For wires under the same load and made of the same material, $
$$\Delta l=\dfrac{FL}{\pi r^2Y},\qquad \dfrac{\Delta l_P}{\Delta l_Q}=\dfrac{0.6}{0.9}\left(\dfrac{0.6}{0.4}\right)^2=\dfrac{3}{2}.$$
